The '''Kapinawá language''' is a presumed and unattested language of northeastern Brazil, formerly spoken by the [[Kapinawá]], who are now monolingual in Portuguese. As Kapinawá is unattested, it cannot be shown to have been distinct from neighboring languages.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Hammarström |first=Harald |date=September 2015 |title=Ethnologue 16/17/18th editions: A comprehensive review: Online appendices |url=https://muse.jhu.edu/article/593411 |journal=Language |language=en |volume=91 |issue=3 |pages=s1–s188 |doi=10.1353/lan.2015.0049 |issn=1535-0665|hdl=11858/00-001M-0000-0029-1D58-0 |hdl-access=free |url-access=subscription }}</ref> The Kapinawá are said to be descended from the Paratió, who spoke the [[Paratió language]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Kapinawá - UFPE |url=https://www.ufpe.br/nepe/povos-indigenas/kapinawa |access-date=2023-03-30 |website=www.ufpe.br}}</ref>
